pattern_explanation: The Polish word and its English look-alike share a close form, so learners may assume the English word carries the same meaning. The English word has a different meaning, so the learner has to map the Polish word to its true English equivalent.
false_friend_warning: Warning: the Polish word 'monitor' means a computer screen, but the English verb 'monitor' means to watch or track something over time, as in monitoring online activity. Similarly, the English word 'actual' does not mean the Polish word 'aktualny' (current); 'actual' means real or existing. Also, 'eventually' means in the end, not 'possibly'.
